advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have `_intersect_capabilities` propagate a `cache_min_prefix_tokens` (e.g. `max(c.cache_min_prefix_tokens for c in per_candidate)`) so a fallback chain uses the conservative per-model floor instead of the blanket 4096 default.
evidence: capabilities.py:118 `cache_min_prefix_tokens: int = CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (default 4096) — so the intersect result always carries 4096
runner.py:392 `caps = _intersect_capabilities([capabilities_for(m) for m in model.models])` then runner.py:504 passes `cache_min_prefix_tokens=caps.cache_min_prefix_tokens` into the warning

runner.py:628 when all candidates share the style, `prompt_cache_style` is preserved (e.g. 'anthropic'), so `cache_settings` is non-None and `caching_requested=True` — the warning path is live, not short-circuited
ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/test_cache_floor_per_model.py exercises `_intersect_capabilities` / the fallback-chain floor
advisory.finding: `_intersect_capabilities` builds a `ModelCapabilities` for a fallback chain without setting `cache_min_prefix_tokens`, so it falls back to the field default 4096 even when every candidate shares a lower documented floor. For a homogeneous anthropic fallback chain (caching IS requested), `warn_if_cache_ineffective` then receives 4096 instead of the true per-model floor — reintroducing the e3cd false-negative (a real caching failure with a 1024–4096-token marked prefix is silently swallowed) on the fallback path.
scenarios: A FallbackModel chain of same-style anthropic Claude models (e.g. sonnet-4-6 primary + sonnet-4-6-ish fallback, real floor 1024) where a 1500-token marked prefix reports zero/zero — should warn under e3cd but stays silent because the chain floor is 4096.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `cache_min_prefix_tokens=max(c.cache_min_prefix_tokens for c in per_candidate)` to the `ModelCapabilities(...)` returned by `_intersect_capabilities` (max is the conservative, warn-suppressing choice consistent with the chain's other fields).

advisory.finding: The new public function `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` (src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:504), which is the production seam wiring this whole feature into `runner.py:501`, has zero direct test coverage across all three of its return branches. Every `warn_if_cache_ineffective` test injects `marked_prefix_tokens` as a literal, so the estimator's logic never executes under test: a regression that inverts the instructions-key check, mishandles the falsy `cache_settings` guard, or returns `None` when a breakpoint IS set would silently route every real call back to the old total-input predicate — defeating the fix — while all 17 tests in the new file remain green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add table-driven tests: (1) `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens(None, system_prompt='...') is None`; (2) `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens({}, ...) is None`; (3) `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens({'anthropic_cache_instructions': True}, system_prompt=s) == est_tokens(s)` and the same for `bedrock_cache_instructions`; (4) a settings dict with only tool_definitions/messages keys set but no instructions breakpoint -> None.
